claim: UNC-8 is a DEG/ENaC cation channel protein.
source: Here we show that the C. elegans Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel (DEG/ENaC) protein, UNC-8, is transcriptionally controlled to function as a trigger in an activity-dependent mechanism that removes synapses in remodeling GABAergic neurons.
evidence: Stated directly in the abstract as a characterization of UNC-8.

claim: UNC-8 is transcriptionally controlled to function as a trigger in an activity-dependent mechanism that removes synapses in remodeling GABAergic neurons.
source: Here we show that the C. elegans Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channel (DEG/ENaC) protein, UNC-8, is transcriptionally controlled to function as a trigger in an activity-dependent mechanism that removes synapses in remodeling GABAergic neurons.
evidence: This is the main finding of the study as stated in the abstract.

claim: UNC-8 cation channel activity promotes disassembly of presynaptic domains in DD type GABA neurons.
source: UNC-8 cation channel activity promotes disassembly of presynaptic domains in DD type GABA neurons, but not in VD class GABA neurons where unc-8 expression is blocked by the COUP/TF transcription factor, UNC-55.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract as a key finding.

claim: unc-8 expression is blocked in VD class GABA neurons by the COUP/TF transcription factor, UNC-55.
source: UNC-8 cation channel activity promotes disassembly of presynaptic domains in DD type GABA neurons, but not in VD class GABA neurons where unc-8 expression is blocked by the COUP/TF transcription factor, UNC-55.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract.

claim: The depolarizing effect of UNC-8-dependent sodium import elevates intracellular calcium in a positive feedback loop involving UNC-2 and TAX-6/calcineurin.
source: We propose that the depolarizing effect of UNC-8-dependent sodium import elevates intracellular calcium in a positive feedback loop involving the voltage-gated calcium channel UNC-2 and the calcium-activated phosphatase TAX-6/calcineurin to initiate a caspase-dependent mechanism that disassembles the presynaptic apparatus.
evidence: This is a proposed model based on the experimental findings.

claim: UNC-2 is a voltage-gated calcium channel.
source: We propose that the depolarizing effect of UNC-8-dependent sodium import elevates intracellular calcium in a positive feedback loop involving the voltage-gated calcium channel UNC-2 and the calcium-activated phosphatase TAX-6/calcineurin to initiate a caspase-dependent mechanism that disassembles the presynaptic apparatus.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract.

claim: TAX-6 is a calcium-activated phosphatase (calcineurin).
source: We propose that the depolarizing effect of UNC-8-dependent sodium import elevates intracellular calcium in a positive feedback loop involving the voltage-gated calcium channel UNC-2 and the calcium-activated phosphatase TAX-6/calcineurin to initiate a caspase-dependent mechanism that disassembles the presynaptic apparatus.
evidence: Directly stated in the abstract.

claim: A caspase-dependent mechanism disassembles the presynaptic apparatus in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: We propose that the depolarizing effect of UNC-8-dependent sodium import elevates intracellular calcium in a positive feedback loop involving the voltage-gated calcium channel UNC-2 and the calcium-activated phosphatase TAX-6/calcineurin to initiate a caspase-dependent mechanism that disassembles the presynaptic apparatus.
evidence: Stated as part of the proposed model in the abstract.

claim: UNC-8 serves as a link between genetic and activity-dependent pathways that promote elimination of GABA synapses in remodeling neurons.
source: Thus, UNC-8 serves as a link between genetic and activity-dependent pathways that function together to promote the elimination of GABA synapses in remodeling neurons.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract.

claim: Calcium influx by voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) triggers neurotransmitter secretion in active neurons.
source: Calcium influx by voltage-gated calcium channels (VGCCs) triggers neurotransmitter secretion in active neurons (Catterall et al., 2008).
evidence: Stated with citation to support the claim.

claim: Elevated intracellular calcium can regulate synaptic strength by controlling gene expression and protein function.
source: Elevated intracellular calcium can also regulate synaptic strength by controlling gene expression and protein function (Flavell and Greenberg, 2008; Baumgärtel and Mansuy, 2012).
evidence: Stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Calcineurin antagonizes long term potentiation (LTP) through dephosphorylation of an AMPA receptor subunit that results in its endocytosis from the postsynaptic membrane.

evidence: Stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: Functional synaptic components can be removed by the canonical apoptotic protease, caspase-3.

claim: CED-3/caspase-3 and CED-4/Apaf1 promote synaptic disassembly by activating the F-actin severing protein gelsolin in C. elegans.
source: In C. elegans, the cell death pathway component CED-3/caspase-3 and its upstream regulator CED-4/Apaf1 promote synaptic disassembly by activating the F-actin severing protein gelsolin; the calcium sensitivity of this pathway points to a potential role for neuronal activity in synaptic remodeling (Pinan-Lucarre et al., 2012; Meng et al., 2015; Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: DEG/ENaCs are voltage-insensitive, trimeric cation channels.
source: Degenerin/Epithelial Sodium Channels (DEG/ENaCs) are voltage-insensitive, trimeric cation channels.

source: The term degenerin arises from the finding that constitutively active forms of DEG/ENaC channels induce neurodegeneration (Bianchi and Driscoll, 2002).
evidence: Stated with citation to support the claim.

claim: ENaCs are expressed in mammalian epithelial tissues, where they promote sodium reabsorption.

evidence: Stated with citations to support the claim.

claim: The depolarizing activity of a presynaptic ENaC channel is proposed to enhance neurotransmitter release by elevating calcium import at local VGCCs.
source: In this case, the depolarizing activity of a presynaptic ENaC channel is proposed to enhance neurotransmitter release by elevating calcium import at local VGCCs (Younger et al., 2013).

claim: VD neurons relocate synapses to the dorsal side in loss-of-function unc-55 mutants.

claim: unc-8 is required for the complete removal of ventral GABA synapses in remodeling DD neurons.

source: In this case, SNB-1::GFP puncta are efficiently removed from the ventral nerve cord, thus confirming that unc-8 exerts a cell-autonomous role in the disassembly of ventral GABAergic synapses (Figure 3—figure supplement 2A).

claim: UNC-8 is required for the efficient removal of the ventral presynaptic apparatus.
source: To summarize, we have shown that unc-55 animals lack GABAergic neuromuscular junctions and that presynaptic components are partially restored in unc-55; unc-8 mutants. Despite the presence of both presynaptic domains with abundant synaptic vesicles and clusters of postsynaptic GABAA receptors, residual GABAergic synapses in unc-55; unc-8 animals are not functional. Taken together, these results indicate that UNC-8 is required for the efficient removal of the ventral presynaptic apparatus, but that the presynaptic defect of unc-55; unc-8 animals could be due to an additional UNC-8-independent pathway, potentially involving the previously described homeodomain transcription factor irx-1 (Petersen et al., 2011), acting in parallel to promote the disassembly of the ventral synaptic architecture of remodeling GABAergic neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the results.

claim: The presynaptic defect of unc-55; unc-8 animals could be due to an additional UNC-8-independent pathway acting in parallel to promote the disassembly of the ventral synaptic architecture of remodeling GABAergic neurons.

evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the data.

claim: Treatment with Amiloride antagonizes the removal of ventral SNB-1::GFP puncta in unc-55 mutant neurons.
source: Treatment with Amiloride also antagonizes the removal of ventral SNB-1::GFP puncta in unc-55 mutant neurons (Figure 5B), but does not alter ventral SNB-1::GFP puncta in either unc-8 or unc-55;unc-8 animals (Figure 5—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in figures.

claim: Amiloride and Benzamil disrupt the GABA neuron synaptic removal due to the inhibition of sodium transport by an UNC-8-containing DEG/ENaC channel.
source: Taken together, these results show that Amiloride and Benzamil disrupt the GABA neuron synaptic removal and are consistent with the idea that this effect is due to the inhibition of sodium transport by an UNC-8-containing DEG/ENaC channel (Figure 5E).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the pharmacological experiments.

claim: Neuronal activity promotes DD presynaptic remodeling.
source: Previous work has shown that neuronal activity promotes DD presynaptic remodeling; the dorsal DD synapse formation is accelerated in mutants that enhance synaptic activity and delayed by genetic defects that block neurotransmission (Thompson-Peer et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citation to previous work.

claim: The dorsal DD synapse formation is accelerated in mutants that enhance synaptic activity and delayed by genetic defects that block neurotransmission.
source: Previous work has shown that neuronal activity promotes DD presynaptic remodeling; the dorsal DD synapse formation is accelerated in mutants that enhance synaptic activity and delayed by genetic defects that block neurotransmission (Thompson-Peer et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated with citation to previous work.

claim: The unc-2 gene encodes a CaV2 α1 subunit of a P/Q-type calcium channel.
source: In C. elegans, the unc-2 gene encodes a CaV2 α1 subunit of a P/Q-type calcium channel (Mathews et al., 2003).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: UNC-2 is localized to the presynaptic terminals of ventral cord motor neurons and is required for neurotransmitter release.
source: UNC-2 is localized to the presynaptic terminals of ventral cord motor neurons and is required for neurotransmitter release (Gracheva et al., 2008; Saheki and Bargmann, 2009).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: unc-55; unc-2 double mutants show a significantly greater number of SNB-1::GFP puncta on the ventral side in comparison to unc-55 animals.
source: We determined that unc-55; unc-2 double mutants show a significantly greater number of SNB-1::GFP puncta on the ventral side in comparison to unc-55 animals (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Wild-type unc-2 promotes synapse removal in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: This result indicates that wild-type unc-2 promotes synapse removal in remodeling GABA neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiment.

claim: No additional increase in the number of ventral cord SNB-1::GFP puncta was observed in unc-55; unc-8; unc-2 animals compared to either double mutant (i.e., unc-55;unc-8 or unc-55;unc-2).
source: We observed no additional increase in the number of ventral cord SNB-1::GFP puncta in unc-55; unc-8; unc-2 animals compared to either double mutant (i.e., unc-55;unc-8 or unc-55;unc-2).
evidence: Stated in the text.

claim: unc-2 and unc-8 act together in a linear pathway to remove ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: This result favors a model in which unc-2 and unc-8 act together in a linear pathway to remove ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons (Figure 6A,B,E).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic epistasis experiment.

claim: The tomosyn protein, TOM-1, normally down-regulates neurotransmitter release by inhibiting synaptic vesicle (SV) priming.
source: The tomosyn protein, TOM-1, normally down-regulates neurotransmitter release by inhibiting synaptic vesicle (SV) priming (Gracheva et al., 2006; McEwen, 2006).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: A loss-of-function tom-1/tomosyn mutant, which enhances evoked SV fusion, results in precocious assembly of dorsal DD synapses.
source: We confirmed that a loss-of-function tom-1/tomosyn mutant, which enhances evoked SV fusion, results in precocious assembly of dorsal DD synapses (Figure 6C) (Thompson-Peer et al., 2012).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6C with citation.

claim: The precocious assembly of dorsal DD synapses in tom-1 mutants was not observed in tom-1;unc-8 double mutants.
source: This effect was not observed, however, in tom-1;unc-8 double mutants which suggests that wild-type unc-8 function is necessary for the accelerated remodeling of DD neurons in tom-1 mutant animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: Stated in the text with reference to figure.

claim: Wild-type unc-8 function is necessary for the accelerated remodeling of DD neurons in tom-1 mutant animals.
source: This effect was not observed, however, in tom-1;unc-8 double mutants which suggests that wild-type unc-8 function is necessary for the accelerated remodeling of DD neurons in tom-1 mutant animals (Figure 6C).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiment.

claim: Optogenetic activation of GABA neurons accelerates DD remodeling.
source: The results of this experiment show that optogenetic activation of GABA neurons accelerates DD remodeling and that both blue light and exogenous all-trans retinal (ATR) are required for this effect; DD neurons that express ChR2 (GABA::ChR2) remodel earlier with significantly more dorsal puncta after 13 hr of light exposure in comparison to controls (Figure 6D).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 6D.

claim: Both blue light and exogenous all-trans retinal (ATR) are required for the optogenetic effect on DD remodeling.
source: The results of this experiment show that optogenetic activation of GABA neurons accelerates DD remodeling and that both blue light and exogenous all-trans retinal (ATR) are required for this effect; DD neurons that express ChR2 (GABA::ChR2) remodel earlier with significantly more dorsal puncta after 13 hr of light exposure in comparison to controls (Figure 6D).
evidence: Stated in the text with reference to figure.

claim: Neuronal activity in DD neurons is sufficient to drive synaptic remodeling.
source: This finding argues that neuronal activity in DD neurons is sufficient to drive synaptic remodeling and thus suggests that a mechanism linking neural activity and unc-8 function could be cell autonomous to GABA neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the optogenetics experiment.

claim: A mechanism linking neural activity and unc-8 function could be cell autonomous to GABA neurons.
source: This finding argues that neuronal activity in DD neurons is sufficient to drive synaptic remodeling and thus suggests that a mechanism linking neural activity and unc-8 function could be cell autonomous to GABA neurons.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the optogenetics results.

claim: Calcineurin is highly expressed throughout the nervous system and has been implicated in activity-dependent mechanisms that regulate synaptic maintenance and function.
source: One of these candidate downstream effectors, the calcium/calmodulin-activated phosphatase, calcineurin, is highly expressed throughout the nervous system and has been implicated in activity-dependent mechanisms that regulate synaptic maintenance and function (Baumäartel and Mansuy, 2012; Winder et al., 1998).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: Calcineurin is composed of two protein components, the catalytic subunit calcineurin A and the regulatory subunit calcineurin B.
source: Calcineurin is composed of two protein components, the catalytic subunit calcineurin A and the regulatory subunit calcineurin B.
evidence: Stated as a characterization of calcineurin.

claim: A tax-6 loss-of-function allele impedes the removal of ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: We found that a tax-6 loss-of-function allele impedes the removal of ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons (Figure 7B).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7B.

claim: A translational reporter gene, ptax-6::TAX-6::GFP is co-localized with the GABA neuron-specific marker, punc-47::mCherry.
source: To ask if tax-6 is expressed in GABA neurons, we determined that a translational reporter gene, ptax-6::TAX-6::GFP is co-localized with the GABA neuron-specific marker, punc-47::mCherry (Figure 7C).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7C.

claim: cnb-1 function is required for the efficient removal of ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: Our results indicate that cnb-1 function is required for the efficient removal of ventral synapses in remodeling GABA neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiment.

claim: Genetic ablation of unc-8 in unc-55; cnb-1 animals do not enhance the remodeling phenotype.
source: In addition, genetic ablation of unc-8 in unc-55; cnb-1 animals do not enhance this phenotype, which suggests that UNC-8 and calcineurin promote synapse elimination in a common pathway (Figure 7D).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7D.

claim: UNC-8 and calcineurin promote synapse elimination in a common pathway.
source: In addition, genetic ablation of unc-8 in unc-55; cnb-1 animals do not enhance this phenotype, which suggests that UNC-8 and calcineurin promote synapse elimination in a common pathway (Figure 7D).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic epistasis experiment.

claim: DD ventral synapses are removed prematurely in tax-6(d) mutants.
source: To test this idea, we used the presynaptic marker GFP::RAB-3 to determine that DD ventral synapses are removed prematurely in tax-6(d) mutants; dorsal synaptic assembly is also precocious and occurs significantly earlier than in wild-type controls.
evidence: Stated in the text.

claim: Dorsal synaptic assembly is precocious in tax-6(d) mutants and occurs significantly earlier than in wild-type controls.
source: To test this idea, we used the presynaptic marker GFP::RAB-3 to determine that DD ventral synapses are removed prematurely in tax-6(d) mutants; dorsal synaptic assembly is also precocious and occurs significantly earlier than in wild-type controls.
evidence: Stated in the text.

claim: Treatment of tax-6(d) animals with the DEG/ENaC inhibitor Benzamil significantly delays the precocious remodeling phenotype.
source: Additionally, we determined that treatment of tax-6(d) animals with the DEG/ENaC inhibitor Benzamil significantly delays the precocious remodeling phenotype (Figure 7E).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 7E.

claim: Intracellular calcium acting through TAX-6/Calcineurin promotes the overall synaptic remodeling mechanism and this effect requires UNC-8 channel activity.
source: These results argue that intracellular calcium acting through TAX-6/Calcineurin promotes the overall synaptic remodeling mechanism and that this effect requires UNC-8 channel activity, thereby suggesting that unc-8 functions downstream of tax-6.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic and pharmacological experiments.

claim: unc-8 functions downstream of tax-6.
source: These results argue that intracellular calcium acting through TAX-6/Calcineurin promotes the overall synaptic remodeling mechanism and that this effect requires UNC-8 channel activity, thereby suggesting that unc-8 functions downstream of tax-6.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the results.

claim: The canonical apoptotic pathway promotes the removal of ventral GABA synapses in remodeling DD neurons.
source: Previous work has shown that the canonical apoptotic pathway promotes the removal of ventral GABA synapses in remodeling DD neurons.
evidence: Stated with reference to previous work.

claim: The adaptor protein CED-4/Apaf1 and its downstream effector, CED-3/caspase activate the actin-severing protein gelsolin to destabilize a presynaptic F-actin network during synapse elimination.
source: In this mechanism, the adaptor protein CED-4/Apaf1 and its downstream effector, CED-3/caspase activate the actin-severing protein gelsolin to destabilize a presynaptic F-actin network during synapse elimination (Meng et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: A loss-of-function mutation in ced-4 results in significant retention of ventral GABA synapses in comparison to unc-55 mutant animals.
source: A loss-of-function mutation in ced-4 results in significant retention of ventral GABA synapses in comparison to unc-55 mutant animals and therefore confirms that ced-4 is necessary for the efficient removal of ventral synapses in both classes (e.g., DD and VD) of remodeling GABA neurons (Figure 8A, [Meng et al., 2015]).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8A with citation.

claim: ced-4 is necessary for the efficient removal of ventral synapses in both classes (e.g., DD and VD) of remodeling GABA neurons.
source: A loss-of-function mutation in ced-4 results in significant retention of ventral GABA synapses in comparison to unc-55 mutant animals and therefore confirms that ced-4 is necessary for the efficient removal of ventral synapses in both classes (e.g., DD and VD) of remodeling GABA neurons (Figure 8A, [Meng et al., 2015]).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic experiment.

claim: The combination of ced-4 and unc-8 mutants did not further enhance the restoration of ventral synapses over that of either unc-55; unc-8 or unc-55; ced-4 animals.
source: Furthermore, the combination of ced-4 and unc-8 mutants did not further enhance the restoration of ventral synapses over that of either unc-55; unc-8 or unc-55; ced-4 animals (Figure 8A).
evidence: Stated in the text and shown in Figure 8A.

claim: The DEG/ENaC protein UNC-8 functions in a common pathway with ced-4 to eliminate ventral GABA synapses.
source: Together, these results suggest that the DEG/ENaC protein UNC-8 functions in a common pathway with ced-4 to eliminate ventral GABA synapses.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the genetic epistasis experiment.

claim: A rise in intracellular calcium in active GABA neurons is sufficient to trigger ced-4-dependent synapse elimination.
source: Because we have also shown that calcium and unc-8 function in a common pathway to promote removal of GABA synapses, we propose that a rise in intracellular calcium in active GABA neurons is sufficient to trigger ced-4-dependent synapse elimination (Figure 8B, see Discussion).
evidence: Stated as a proposal based on the results.

claim: UNC-8 is a member of the conserved DEG/ENaC family of cation channel proteins.
source: In this study, we show that a member of the conserved DEG/ENaC family of cation channel proteins, UNC-8, is transcriptionally controlled to mediate an activity-dependent pathway that promotes the removal of GABAergic synapses in C. elegans.
evidence: Stated in the Discussion section.

claim: Members of the ASIC (acid-sensing ion channels) class of the DEG/ENaC family proteins are activated by low pH and have been implicated in learning and memory.
source: For example, members of the ASIC (acid-sensing ion channels) class of the DEG/ENaC family proteins are activated by low pH and have been implicated in learning and memory (Wemmie et al., 2002, 2004; Zha et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: Acidification of the synaptic cleft that accompanies the neurotransmitter release is thought to trigger ASIC-mediated sodium influx.
source: In one possible mechanism to explain this role, acidification of the synaptic cleft that accompanies the neurotransmitter release is thought to trigger ASIC-mediated sodium influx.
evidence: Stated as a proposed mechanism.

claim: A reconstituted UNC-8 channel is inhibited by low pH.
source: Our finding that a reconstituted UNC-8 channel is in fact inhibited by low pH, however, suggests that UNC-8 is unlikely to function as an ASIC-like protein in vivo (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with citation to previous work.

claim: UNC-8 is unlikely to function as an ASIC-like protein in vivo.
source: Our finding that a reconstituted UNC-8 channel is in fact inhibited by low pH, however, suggests that UNC-8 is unlikely to function as an ASIC-like protein in vivo (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the pH sensitivity data.

claim: The DEG/ENaC protein, pickpocket, exerts a homeostatic function that maintains neurotransmitter release at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction.
source: A recent study established that the DEG/ENaC protein, pickpocket, exerts a homeostatic function that maintains neurotransmitter release at the Drosophila neuromuscular junction.
evidence: Stated as a reference to a recent study.

claim: Sodium influx arising from elevated pickpocket transcription and membrane insertion is proposed to result in local depolarization that activates a nearby voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) and consequent neurotransmitter release.
source: In this mechanism, sodium influx arising from elevated pickpocket transcription and membrane insertion is proposed to result in local depolarization that activates a nearby voltage-gated calcium channel (VGCC) and consequent neurotransmitter release (Younger et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a proposed mechanism with citation.

claim: The CaV2.1 VGCC channel subunit cacophony is required for synaptic homeostasis.
source: This model is consistent with the finding that the CaV2.1 VGCC channel subunit cacophony is required for synaptic homeostasis (Müller and Davis, 2012).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: UNC-8 ultimately eliminates neurotransmitter secretion by triggering destruction of the presynaptic apparatus.
source: Our results are suggestive of a similar presynaptic role for UNC-8 of enhancing intracellular calcium influx with the important difference that UNC-8 ultimately eliminates neurotransmitter secretion by triggering destruction of the presynaptic apparatus.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the results.

claim: UNC-8 preferentially transports sodium and is impermeant to calcium.
source: This UNC-8 function requires its intrinsic cation channel activity (Figure 5) which likely involves sodium influx since electrophysiological studies of a reconstituted UNC-8 channel in Xenopus oocytes indicate that UNC-8 preferentially transports sodium and is impermeant to calcium (Wang et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated with citation to previous work.

claim: UNC-8-dependent sodium import would activate nearby VGCC channels.
source: Because our evidence points to punctate UNC-8 localization within the ventral nerve cord (Figure 2F), it is reasonable to predict that UNC-8-dependent sodium import would activate nearby VGCC channels (Wemmie et al., 2013).
evidence: Stated as a prediction based on the data.

claim: VGCC function is required for ASIC-induced elevation of intracellular calcium in hippocampal neurons.
source: This idea is consistent with the observation that VGCC function is required for ASIC-induced elevation of intracellular calcium in hippocampal neurons (Zha et al., 2006).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: UNC-2 mediates calcium influx to drive neurotransmitter release.
source: As a key component of the presynaptic apparatus, UNC-2 mediates calcium influx to drive neurotransmitter release (Richmond et al., 2001).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: The UNC-2-dependent rise in cytoplasmic calcium in active GABA neurons is enhanced by UNC-8 cation channel function.
source: We suggest that the UNC-2-dependent rise in cytoplasmic calcium in active GABA neurons is enhanced by UNC-8 cation channel function.
evidence: Stated as a suggestion based on the results.

claim: The elevation of intracellular calcium arising from the interaction between UNC-2 and UNC-8 could be required for efficient removal of the presynaptic apparatus in remodeling GABA neurons.
source: Moreover, because our genetic results indicate that unc-2 and unc-8 function in a common pathway (Figure 6A), the elevation of intracellular calcium arising from this interaction could be required for efficient removal of the presynaptic apparatus in remodeling GABA neurons (see below).
evidence: Stated as a speculation based on the genetic results.

claim: Calcineurin/CaN antagonizes LTP in a mechanism that dephosphorylates the GluR1 subunit of the AMPA receptor to promote its removal from the postsynaptic membrane.
source: For example, calcineurin/CaN antagonizes LTP in a mechanism that dephosphorylates the GluR1 subunit of the AMPA receptor to promote its removal from the postsynaptic membrane (Winder et al., 1998; Gorski et al., 2012; Lee et al., 1998).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: TAX-6/Calcineurin could exert a parallel role in the removal of the presynaptic apparatus in GABA neurons by activating the UNC-8 channel.
source: TAX-6/Calcineurin could exert a parallel role in the removal of the presynaptic apparatus in GABA neurons by activating the UNC-8 channel.
evidence: Stated as a speculation.

claim: The DEG/ENaC inhibitor, Benzamil, potently blocks the accelerated remodeling phenotype of a constitutively active TAX-6 protein.
source: Our finding that the DEG/ENaC inhibitor, Benzamil, potently blocks the accelerated remodeling phenotype of a constitutively active TAX-6 protein is consistent with this idea (Figure 7E).
evidence: Stated in the text with reference to figure.

claim: The resultant positive feedback loop involving UNC-2, TAX-6/Calcineurin and UNC-8 should further elevate intracellular calcium.
source: The resultant positive feedback loop involving UNC-2, TAX-6/Calcineurin and UNC-8 should further elevate intracellular calcium (Figure 8).
evidence: Stated as a prediction based on the model.

claim: Phosphorylation by CaMKII activates ASIC1a and the resultant VGCC-dependent elevation of intracellular calcium in turn promotes CaMKII activity.
source: In an analogous mechanism, phosphorylation by CaMKII activates ASIC1a and the resultant VGCC-dependent elevation of intracellular calcium in turn promotes CaMKII activity (Zha et al., 2006; Gao et al., 2005; Zha and Zha, 2013).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: UNC-8 would act as a synaptic amplifier to drive a self-reinforcing signaling pathway that elevates intracellular calcium.
source: In this model, UNC-8 would act as a synaptic amplifier to drive a self-reinforcing signaling pathway that elevates intracellular calcium.
evidence: Stated as part of the proposed model.

claim: Both CED-3 and gelsolin function in calcium-dependent pathways.
source: Notably, both CED-3 and gelsolin function in calcium-dependent pathways (Pinan-Lucarre et al., 2012; Liu et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with citations.

claim: UNC-8 promotes the elevation of intracellular calcium above a critical threshold that then triggers the apoptotic pathway to dismantle the presynaptic region.
source: Because our genetic evidence argues that unc-8 and ced-4 function in a common pathway (Figure 8A), we propose a model in which UNC-8 promotes the elevation of intracellular calcium above a critical threshold that then triggers the apoptotic pathway to dismantle the presynaptic region.
evidence: Stated as a proposed model based on the genetic results.

claim: The localization of apoptotic components to the presynaptic membrane may ensure that a local rise in calcium near the synapse is sufficient to activate this mechanism, but also protects the neuron from apoptotic death.
source: The localization of apoptotic components to the presynaptic membrane (Meng et al., 2015) may ensure that a local rise in calcium near the synapse is sufficient to activate this mechanism, but also protects the neuron from apoptotic death.
evidence: Stated as a speculation with citation.

claim: The conserved role of CED-3/caspase-3 in synapse elimination in other species argues that similar DEG/ENaC-dependent mechanisms could be widely employed to trigger synaptic destruction.
source: The conserved role of CED-3/caspase-3 in synapse elimination in other species (Ertürk et al., 2014; Wang et al., 2014;Li et al., 2010) argues that similar DEG/ENaC-dependent mechanisms could be widely employed to trigger synaptic destruction.
evidence: Stated as a speculation based on conservation with citations.

claim: unc-8 promotes the removal of ventral synapses in remodeling DD and VD motor neurons, but is generally not necessary for the nascent assembly of dorsal synapses.
source: Our results show that unc-8 promotes the removal of ventral synapses in remodeling DD and VD motor neurons, but is generally not necessary for the nascent assembly of dorsal synapses (Figure 2E).
evidence: Stated as a summary of the results.

claim: The proposed downstream role of the apoptotic pathway is limited to synaptic removal.
source: The proposed downstream role of the apoptotic pathway is similarly limited to synaptic removal (Meng et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: The elimination of GABAergic synapses is only partially dependent on the unc-8 pathway.
source: In addition, the elimination of GABAergic synapses is only partially dependent on this unc-8 pathway (Figure 2C, Figure 3, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A, Figure 4) (Meng et al., 2015).
evidence: Stated with references to figures and citation.

claim: The cyclin box-containing protein CYY-1 and cyclin-dependent kinase CDK-5 function together to promote synaptic removal and reassembly, respectively.
source: For example, the cyclin box-containing protein CYY-1 and cyclin-dependent kinase CDK-5 function together to promote synaptic removal and reassembly, respectively (Park et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: The Iroquois family homeodomain transcription factor, IRX-1, promotes synaptic removal.
source: In previous work, we have shown that the Iroquois family homeodomain transcription factor, IRX-1, promotes synaptic removal.
evidence: Stated with reference to previous work.

claim: IRX-1 also promotes dorsal DD synapse formation, suggesting that IRX-1 orchestrates expression of multiple genes that drive DD synaptic remodeling.
source: IRX-1 also promotes dorsal DD synapse formation, suggesting that IRX-1 orchestrates expression of multiple genes that drive DD synaptic remodeling (Petersen et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: Functional GABA synapses are restored to the ventral nerve cord of unc-55 animals that are also mutant for irx-1.
source: The exact function of the IRX-1 pathway in synaptic disassembly is unknown, but likely involves the extraction of components that are required for GABA release since functional GABA synapses are restored to the ventral nerve cord of unc-55 animals that are also mutant for irx-1 (Petersen et al., 2011).
evidence: Stated with citation.

claim: UNC-8 alone is sufficient to trigger synapse elimination.
source: Despite the necessity for additional pathways functioning in parallel to unc-8 to execute a comprehensive GABA neuron remodeling program, our results also determined that UNC-8 alone is sufficient to trigger synapse elimination (Figure 3—figure supplement 2B).
evidence: Stated with reference to figure.

claim: Transcriptional regulation of unc-8 expression effectively functions as a genetic switch that determines the developmental fate of the presynaptic signaling apparatus in active GABAergic neurons.
source: This finding argues that transcriptional regulation of unc-8 expression effectively functions as a genetic switch that determines the developmental fate of the presynaptic signaling apparatus in active GABAergic neurons.
evidence: Stated as a conclusion from the sufficiency experiment.
